```
    at Function.keys (native)
    at Object.deepmerge [as merge] (/Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-ops.js:175:20)
    at getLocalConfig (/Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config.js:147:71)
    at Config.getConfig (/Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config.js:222:22)
    at processText (/Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine.js:155:27)
    at processFile (/Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine.js:227:18)
    at executeOnFile (/Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine.js:603:23)
    at /Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine.js:630:17
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at CLIEngine.executeOnFiles (/Users/denny/Development/react-simple-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine.js:625:18)
```

After investigating a little bit I think the error cause is in `./lib/config/config-file.js` function `loadPackageJSONConfigFile` row 175:

```
return loadJSONConfigFile(filePath).eslintConfig || null;
```

Than the fix for the mentioned error would simply be:

```
return loadJSONConfigFile(filePath).eslintConfig || {};
```

But of course I don't overlook other dependend components, which may fail in turn...
Thanks. Looks like we missed no config scenario.
@dchowitz - Would you like to submit a PR for the fix?
IIRC something was depending on that `null`, so not sure we just want to swap in an object, but that's likely the area of the problem
Yes, why not. But give me some time (a day or two) - this will be my first PR ever ;-)

> this will be my first PR ever ;-)

Yay! :tada:
Another possibility would be to protect the deepmerge function in config-ops to fallback to empty objects if null/undefined is given for source and/or destination.
I will look into it and come back with a PR...

I think there may be more to this than it seems. I just did a quick local test in a folder without `.eslintrc.*` files and with an empty `package.json` file. This is what I got (using master branch):

```
$ node ../eslint/bin/eslint.js foo.js --debug
  eslint:cli Running on files +0ms
  eslint:ignored-paths Looking for ignore file in C:\Users\Nicholas\projects\personal\tmp +109ms

  eslint:cli-engine Linting complete in: 78ms +47ms
```

So I don't think this is a simple as there being no configuration found, something else must be going on.

@dchowitz can you share your `package.json` file?

This is my `package.json` file:

```

    "uglifyjs": "^2.4.10",

  },
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^0.14.7",
    "react-dom": "^0.14.7"
  }

```

Hmm, nothing interesting in there. :( I tried copying that into my local test case and still couldn't reproduce.

Do you have a file in `~/package.json`? I just noticed the debug log you posted stops there and throws an error, whereas my debug log doesn't follow suit.

Yes, by accident there is an old `~/package.json`, but without `eslintConfig` section. The point is, that `getPersonalConfig` in `config.js` (which is the very last fallback for a config file, if I read the code correctly) is expected (according to its comment) to return an empty object, if no personal config could be found. But in fact it returns `null` in my case, because `~/package.json` doesn't contain the `eslintConfig`.

IMHO `getPersonalConfig` should be fixed.

For the sake of completeness my `~/package.json` - nothing fancy in it:

```
{
  "name": "gulptest",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "description": "",
  "main": "index.js",
  "devDependencies": {
    "gulp": "^3.8.11",
    "gulp-uglify": "^1.1.0",
    "gulp-concat": "^2.5.2",
    "gulp-babel": "^4.0.0",
    "event-stream": "^3.2.2",
    "gulp-sourcemaps": "^1.5.0",
    "del": "^1.1.1",
    "gulp-filesize": "0.0.6",
    "browser-sync": "^2.2.1"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1"
  },
  "author": "denny",
  "license": "ISC"
}
```
I deleted my `~/package.json` file and `eslint app.js` works. So that is definitely the bug's cause.

Okay, so that's the key. It's not _any_ `package.json` file that causes a problem, it's only `~/package.json`. That's an important distinction. I was able to reproduce by doing this.

Yeah, making sure `getPersonalConfig()` always returns an object seems like the best approach.
